sanskrit: āyam agan parṇamaṇir balī balena pramṛṇan sapatnān | ojo devānāṃ paya oṣadhīnāṃ mayi rāṣṭraṃ jinvatv aprayucchan ||
english: Here has come the parṇa-amulet, powerful, crushing rivals by its might; the vigour of the gods, the sap of plants — may it invigorate sovereignty in me without faltering.

sanskrit: mayi rāṣṭraṃ parṇamaṇe mayi dhārayā śriyam | ahaṃ rāṣṭrasyābhīvarge yujā bhūyāsam uttaraḥ ||
english: In me hold sovereignty, O parṇa-amulet; in me establish splendour; may I, in the overlordship of the realm, be allied with you and be supreme.

sanskrit: yaṃ nidadhur vanaspatau vājaṃ devāḥ priyaṃ nidhim | taṃ ma indraḥ sahāyuṣā maṇiṃ dadhātu bhartave ||
english: The prize, the dear hidden treasure, that the gods deposited in a forest tree — may Indra bestow that amulet upon me together with long life, to be worn.

sanskrit: somasya parṇaḥ saha ugram āgann indreṇa datto varuṇena sakhyā | tam ahaṃ bibharmi bahu rocamāno dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya ||
english: The leaf of Soma has come hither with powerful force, given by Indra, in friendship by Varuṇa; I wear it, shining brilliantly in many ways, for long life, for a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: ā mā rukṣat parṇamaṇir mahyā ariṣṭatātaye | yathāham uttaro 'sāni mānuṣyā adhi sampadaḥ ||
english: May the parṇa-amulet cling fast to me for my complete uninjuredness, so that I may be supreme over the human accumulation of riches.

sanskrit: punar maitv indriyaṃ punar ātmā draviṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca | punar agnayo dhiṣṇyāso yathāsthāma kalpayantām ihaiva ||
english: May vital power return to me, may the self, wealth, and the brahman return; may the dhiṣṇya fires arrange themselves back in their proper stations, right here.

sanskrit: ye takṣāṇo rathakārāḥ karmārā ye manīṣiṇaḥ | sarvāṃs tān parṇa randhaya- -upastiṃ kṛṇu me janam ||
english: The carpenters, the chariot-makers, the blacksmiths, and the wise counsellors — subdue them all, O Parṇa; make my people into submissive attendants.

sanskrit: upastir astu vaiśya uta śūdra utāryaḥ | sarvāṃs tān parṇa randhaya- -upastiṃ kṛṇu me janam ||
english: Let there be a submissive attendant whether Vaiśya, or Śūdra, or noble Ārya — subdue them all, O Parṇa; make my people into submissive attendants.

sanskrit: yena vehad babhūvitha nāśayāmasi tad vayam | idaṃ tad anyatra tvad apa dūre ni dadhmasi ||
english: That by which you became a barren woman — that we destroy; this very thing we lay away far from you, elsewhere, at a distance.

sanskrit: ā te garbho yonim etu pumān vāṇa iveṣudhim | ā vīro 'tra jāyatāṃ putras te daśamāsyaḥ ||
english: May an embryo enter your womb, a male, like an arrow into a quiver; may a hero be born here — your son at ten months.

sanskrit: pumāṃsaṃ putraṃ janaya taṃ pumān anu jāyatām | bhavāsi putrāṇāṃ mātā jātānāṃ janayāsi ca ||
english: Bear a male child, a son; after him may another male be born; may you become a mother of sons — of those already born and those yet to be born.

sanskrit: yāni bhadrāṇi bījāny ṛṣabhā janayanti | tais tvaṃ putraṃ vindasva sā prasūr dhenukā bhava ||
english: With the good seeds that bulls engender, find a son for yourself with those; be a prolific cow, a milch-cow.

sanskrit: kṛṇomi te prajāpatyam ā garbho yonim etu te | vindasva putraṃ nāri yas tubhyaṃ śam asac cham u tasmai tvaṃ bhava ||
english: I make for you the Prajāpati rite; may the embryo enter your womb; find a son, O woman — one who shall be a blessing to you, and you in turn shall be a blessing to him.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ pitā parjanyo bhūmir mātā babhūva | tās tvā putravidyāya devīḥ prāvantv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: Those divine plants whose father was Parjanya and whose mother was the Earth — may they, the goddesses, help you toward the finding of a son.

sanskrit: yas te yonim udiṅgayād ṛṣabho retasā saha | sa ta ā siñcatu prajāṃ dīrghāyuṃ śataśāradām ||
english: That bull who shall stir your womb together with his seed — may he pour into you offspring of long life, lasting a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvā vātovarayad ārdranābhā maharṣabhaḥ | tasyās te viśvadhāyaso viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: The plant that the great bull with the moist navel, Vāta, enclosed — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvā varāho akhanad ekasminn adhi puṣkare | tasyās te viśvadhāyaso viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: The plant that the boar rooted up in a single lotus-pond — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvāditir avapad bījavāpam adhi puṣkare | tasyās te viśvadhāyaso viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: The plant that Aditi sowed as seed-sower upon a lotus-pond — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ kulāyaṃ salile antar mahaty arṇave | tasyās te viśvadhāyaso viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: She whose nest is within the waters in the great ocean — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.

sanskrit: ut te bhara uttamāyā adhamāyās ta ud bhare | un madhyamān madhyame tad viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: I bring up for you from the highest; from the lowest I bring up for you; from the middle-ones the middle one — I bring up that poison-neutralizer.

sanskrit: agrabhaṃ sam agrabham ubhāvantau sam agrabham | divaś ca pṛthivyāś ca viṣadūṣaṇam ud bhare ||
english: I seized, together I seized, both ends together I seized; I bring up the poison-neutralizer of heaven and earth.
